title: November flow gave no clear March forecast gain beyond time at Mackenzie in 24 certified winters from 1995 to 2019
abstract: We tested whether November flow improves March log-flow forecasts beyond a time trend at Mackenzie-Arctic Red River. Earlier-year fits used ArcticGRO v20261104. A complete certified sample retained 24 test winters in 1995-2019. November reduced mean squared log-flow error by 6.61%, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of -36.10% to 36.63%. Estimating the November coefficient instead of fixing it at one reduced error by 70.28%, with limits of 51.06% to 80.79%. Thus, the large gain against a proportional model did not establish useful information beyond time. An added autumn-change term gave a 31.35% point gain but block-length-sensitive limits. This adds a separate basin to earlier Siberian tests. A short revised record, regulation, ice effects, model form and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Original code, aggregate draws, an arithmetic audit, source hashes and a figure support reproduction. External source and year-level tables remain outside the package.

display.caption: Paired forecast score contrasts and main model errors. Positive score means lower mean squared log-flow error. Limits use three-year blocks.
